title: Container Bookings: Cancellation of a Confirmed Booking and Its Charges
content:
This page governs the cancellation of a Container Bookings booking after space has been confirmed: which bookings can be cancelled, how the cancellation fee is priced, when it falls away, and what happens to a loading guarantee premium.

## Policy clause

**Who and what.** Cancellation is open to a booking at the confirmed, equipment released or gated in stage, and it is carried out when the verified customer instructs it. A booking that is still at the requested stage is not cancelled but withdrawn, through the confirmation and decline handling, and it never attracts a cancellation fee.

**Pricing.** The cancellation fee is a per-container amount applied to the container quantity of the booking. The per-container amount is chosen by the number of whole calendar days separating the cancellation date from the scheduled departure date: 14 days or more selects the first band, 7 to 13 days the second, 3 to 6 days the third and 0 to 2 days the fourth, each at the product's rate for that band. The day count is the difference between the two calendar dates, the departure date less the cancellation date, with the time of day disregarded; a cancellation made once the scheduled departure date has already gone by falls in the 0 to 2 day band. The fee is therefore the band rate multiplied by the container quantity, or the product's per-booking ceiling where that is lower. Where the fee works out at 0.00, no fee entry is made.

**Relief.** No cancellation fee is charged when the number of carrier-caused rolls recorded on the booking, counted over its whole life, has reached the product's figure for fee-free cancellation. Nor is one charged when the product's line-rejection setting is on and the line has rejected the dangerous-goods acceptance of this booking, as its acceptance record shows. Either relief only removes the fee; neither creates a credit, and the two do not add up to anything more.

**Limits on the entry.** A cancellation fee can be entered only on a booking whose status is cancelled, and one booking can carry no more than one cancellation fee.

**Loading guarantee premium.** If the cancelled booking paid a loading guarantee premium and the cancellation came no fewer than the product's refund-notice days, in calendar days, ahead of the scheduled departure date, the premium entry is refunded in full by a waiver-family entry coded as a premium refund that references that premium entry. A later cancellation leaves the premium with the line. A premium refund is not goodwill and never uses up the customer's goodwill quota.

**Related records.** Cancelling voids the booking's draft transport document. The export free-time record opened for the booking is cancelled only if no empty container has been collected under it.

## Band boundaries (hypothetical dates)

| Calendar days from cancellation date to departure date | Band applied |
|---|---|
| 14 | 14 days or more |
| 13 | 7 to 13 days |
| 7 | 7 to 13 days |
| 6 | 3 to 6 days |
| 3 | 3 to 6 days |
| 2 | 0 to 2 days |
| departure date already passed | 0 to 2 days |

## Worked example (hypothetical rates)

An invented product charges 110.00 per container in the band concerned and has a ceiling of 1000.00. Cancelling 8 containers gives 880.00, which stands; cancelling 12 containers gives 1320.00, which the ceiling reduces to 1000.00. If the same booking had already been rolled by the carrier as many times as the product's fee-free figure, no fee would be entered at all.

## Premium refund boundary (hypothetical)

With a refund notice of 10 days, a cancellation exactly 10 calendar days before departure gets the premium back; one made 9 days before does not.
